title: More, fewer, equal
examples: Teacher, how do I show that one group has more?
If I have three apples and you give me one more, how many do I have?
What does it mean if two groups are equal?

explain.say: Look at these two groups of toys. Can you count them for me?
Group A has three toys. Group B has two toys. Group A has more toys than group B.
Now look at these two groups. One has four blocks and the other has four blocks. They have an equal number of blocks.
Here we have five balls and only two balls. The two balls have fewer balls than the five balls.
If you have three fingers up and I add one more finger, you now have four fingers up. That is one more.

faq.q: What does 'more' mean when we talk about numbers?
faq.a: More means a bigger amount or a larger group of things. You can also ask which group has more.

faq.q: How do I know if two groups are equal?
faq.a: Two groups are equal if they have the exact same number of items. You can count them to check.
Fewer means a smaller amount than what you started with. It means taking some away.

faq.q: If I have five counters and get one more, how many do I have?
faq.a: You count the five counters and then count one more. You will have six counters in total.

faq.q: If I have eight fingers and take two away, how many are left?
faq.a: You start with eight and take away two fingers. You will be left with six fingers.

facts: Comparing groups helps us know which group has the biggest amount.
Equal groups have the same number of items in them.
One more means adding one single item to a group.
One less means taking one single item away from a group.

quiz.say: Which group has more apples, the group with 5 or the group with 3?
quiz.why: Five is a bigger number than three, so it has more.

wrong.0: This is wrong because three is a smaller number than five.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the numbers 5 and 3 are not the same.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you can easily count and compare the groups.

quiz.say: If you have 4 crayons and find 1 more, how many do you have?
quiz.why: Adding one more to four gives you five.

wrong.0: This is wrong because adding one always makes the number bigger.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you only added one, not two.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you added one, so the number must go up.

quiz.say: Which pair of objects shows an equal amount?
quiz.show: Group A: 2 stars, Group B: 2 circles
quiz.why: Equal means they both have the same number of items, which is two.

wrong.0: This is wrong because they both clearly have two items each.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you must compare both groups to see if they match.
wrong.3: This is wrong because both groups look the same size.
